findings.description: The KMS key has no enable_key_rotation = true, so AWS never rotates its backing key material. Long-lived key material increases the impact of any key compromise and fails key-management hygiene for a key protecting audit data. Rotation must be explicitly enabled (and ideally with a customer-managed key policy).

No key policy is defined and no aws_kms_key_policy resource exists, so the key relies on the default account-level policy which grants key administration and usage to the whole account via the root principal. Combined with unrestricted grants, any principal in the account (or any IAM role able to escalate) can use or alter this audit-bucket key. An explicit least-privilege key policy naming only the intended principals is required.
